nodes.description: Without bridges, spermatogonia still proliferate and differentiate, but in lower numbers and out of step with one another. Whether this explains the spermatogonial arrest seen in some patients is open (see the discussion on arrest-stage heterogeneity), so no edge is drawn to that phenotype.

evidence.reference_title: Spermatogonial asynchrony in Tex14 mutant mice lacking intercellular bridges.
evidence.snippet: Thus although spermatogonial development is able to proceed, in the absence of ICBs in Tex14-/- mutants, the yield of cells, specific steps of differentiation, the synchrony of the cell kinetics, and the subsequent progression in meiosis are quantitatively lower than normal.

nodes.description: Dividing spermatogonia and spermatocytes do not form the stable intercellular bridges that normally connect a clone of germ cells into a syncytium. Bridges are absent by electron microscopy and bridge markers in Tex14-null mice and in patient testes, and the cytoplasmic sharing of transcripts between connected germ cells is reduced.

nodes.description: Most reported alleles are truncating. Loss of TEX14 protein has been shown for a compound heterozygous missense and nonsense pair and for a knock-in of a patient frameshift in mice; the splice and missense alleles from the other reports have not been tested. TEX14 is a catalytically inactive kinase-like protein. Its conserved AxGPPx3Y motif binds the EABR domain of CEP55 and competes with ALIX and TSG101, the ESCRT-associated factors that CEP55 recruits to complete abscission in somatic cells.

evidence.reference_title: TEX14 interacts with CEP55 to block cell abscission.
evidence.snippet: an evolutionarily conserved GPPX3Y motif of TEX14 binds strongly to CEP55 to block similar GPPX3Y motifs of ALIX and TSG101 from interacting and localizing to the midbody

evidence.reference_title: Structural and biochemical insights into the role of testis-expressed gene 14 (TEX14) in forming the stable intercellular bridges of germ cells.
evidence.snippet: TEX14 competitively binds to CEP55-EABR to prevent the recruitment of ALIX, which is a component of the ESCRT machinery with the AxGPPx3Y motif.

evidence.reference_title: Germ cell intercellular bridges.
evidence.snippet: TEX14 is an inactive kinase essential for the maintenance of stable intercellular bridges in gametes of both sexes but whose loss specifically impairs male meiosis.

evidence.reference_title: A Novel Compound Heterozygous Mutation in TEX14 Causes Human Non-Obstructive Azoospermia by Disrupting the Assembly of Intercellular Bridges.
evidence.snippet: Functional analyses demonstrated that these mutations disrupted TEX14 synthesis.

evidence.reference_title: Pathogenic TEX14 Variants Disrupt Intercellular Bridge Formation, Causing Meiotic Arrest and Non-Obstructive Azoospermia in Humans and Mice.
evidence.snippet: These mice recapitulated the human NOA phenotype, showing a complete loss of TEX14 expression in the testis.

nodes.description: A knock-in of an allele analogous to a patient frameshift abolishes TEX14 in the testis, prevents bridge formation and arrests spermatogenesis at zygotene, matching the patient's testicular histology.

A hypomorphic allele reduces rather than abolishes bridges. Together with Tex14-null mice it showed failed meiotic DNA replication, synapsis and double-strand break repair, retrotransposon derepression, and reduced transcript sharing between connected germ cells.
Male Tex14 knockout mice lack germ cell intercellular bridges and are sterile, with arrest before the first meiotic division. Females are fertile.
